mutants.description: Student error: the convexity explanation omits the one-expiry label P2 that the convexity finding depends on.
Student error: the parity explanation omits the supplied discount factor label P4 that a parity finding uses.
Student error: parity_gap_cents returns a float from true division, so the cents are not an integer.
Student error: scan runs the convexity test on the put quotes instead of the call quotes.
Parity uses the strike K instead of the discounted strike K df (both entry points).
Parity gap sign flipped: parity_gap_cents returns the negated gap.
Cost charged once per finding (one leg) instead of per leg (three legs).
Costs ignored: gross violations are reported as findings with no cost netting.
Ordering not checked: convexity is computed in the input order of strikes, so shuffled strikes are accepted.
Convexity tested with the first difference: a violation is a call that falls between neighbours, not a second difference.
Rounding by truncation toward zero instead of half up, so an exact half cent goes down in magnitude.
df_ppm read as parts per thousand: the discount factor is df_ppm / 1000.
Net-of-cost rule uses >= 0: a finding whose net amount is exactly zero is kept.
Hard-coded answer: scan returns seed 0's findings for any chain.
Convexity test run on call quotes discounted by df_ppm (P5 says quotes are present values, so no discounting): the gross of a convexity finding is scaled by df.
Convexity chord uses equal weights of one half on the two neighbours, which is wrong on an uneven strike grid.
Gross amount rounded with Python round(), which sends an exact half cent to the even cent, not up.
Convexity scan stops one strike early, so a violation at the last interior strike is never reported.
Student error: df_ppm = 0 accepted, so the range lower bound is off by one (1 to 1000000 is the contract).
Student error: df_ppm = 1000001 accepted, so the range upper bound is off by one.
Student error: parity_gap_cents accepts a strike of zero, because the check uses < instead of <=.
Student error: a call exactly on the chord is flagged, so the test uses <= 0 instead of < 0.
Student error: a finding whose net amount is exactly zero is kept, so the net test uses >= 0 instead of > 0.
Student error: a negative half-spread is accepted, because the cost check only looks at the fee.
Student error: the chord uses equal weights on the two neighbours, which is right only on an even grid.
Student error: the gross of a half-cent tie rounds toward zero, so an exact 2.5 cents gives 2 instead of 3.
Student error: parity records are built from the strikes in reverse order, which breaks the required strike order.
Student error: the quote-length check ignores the put list, so a short put list is not rejected.
Student error: each finding is charged two legs of fee plus half-spread instead of three.
Student error: the convexity gross is floored, so a 0.5-cent or 1.5-cent violation loses its half cent.
Student error: convexity findings are emitted in reverse strike order (the loop walks the indices backwards).
Student error: the convexity explanation omits the European-exercise label P1 it depends on.
Student error: the call is discounted by df in the parity gap, as if it were a payment at expiry.
Student error: the half-spread is charged once per finding while the fee is charged on each of three legs.
Convexity explanation omits the cost label P6 that every cost depends on.
Parity gap discounts the strike by dividing by the discount factor instead of multiplying.
Negative parity gaps are skipped, so only calls rich to the synthetic forward are reported.
Convexity net charges two legs instead of three, so a finding one cost-leg too rich is kept.
Findings returned sorted by net amount, largest first, instead of parity then convexity in strike order.
Student error: the discount factor is rounded to four decimal places before the parity gap is taken.
Student error: the gross of a parity gap is rounded with ceil(magnitude - 1/2), so an exact half cent goes down.
Student error: a convexity finding is netted with two legs of cost, not three, so a finding one leg too rich is kept.
Student error: the convexity explanation omits the present-value label P5 that the convexity finding depends on.
Convexity flags a call exactly on the chord (the test is <= 0, not < 0).
Fee charged once per finding while the half-spread is still paid on each of three legs.
parity_gap_cents accepts a zero or negative strike, which the page names as a ValueError condition.
Gross amount rounded with Python's round() on the float value, which sends a half cent to the even cent.
scan validates the cost terms only inside the finding branch, so a chain with no finding skips the check.
Convexity explanation names P4, the supplied discount factor, which the convexity test does not use.
Parity explanation also names P5 (present-value quotes), which a parity finding does not list.
Convexity explanation names the rule as a chord test and never names convexity.
Convexity chord weights are float quotients passed to Fraction, so a tie at a half cent is not exact.
Convexity returns no violation for a one-strike chain before it checks df_ppm or the strikes.
Convexity checks the quote count only when the chain has at least two strikes.
Convexity chord and its gross are computed in plain float arithmetic, not in exact fractions.
Parity gap and its gross are computed in plain float arithmetic, not in exact fractions.
Student error: each leg charges the fee plus half of the half-spread, so the half-spread is halved a second time.
Student error: the quote-length check tests only that the put list is not shorter, so extra puts are accepted.
Student error: the record's net_cents field carries the gross amount, so the net after cost is never reported.
Student error: the parity explanation labels the supplied discount factor as P5 (the present-value label) instead of P4.
Student error: the discounted strike and the gap are computed in floating point, so an exact half-cent tie can round the wrong way.
Student error: the chord weights are swapped, so each neighbour is weighted by the distance to the wrong end of the grid.
Student error: the parity loop starts at the second strike, so a parity finding at the lowest strike is never reported.
Student error: a parity gap tie is rounded away from zero, so an exact -14.5 cents becomes -15 instead of -14.
Student error: a convexity finding reports the strike of its left neighbour instead of the strike of the middle call.
Student error: a fee of exactly zero is rejected, because the cost check tests for a positive fee instead of a non-negative one.
Student error: the strike check accepts equal neighbouring strikes (b < a instead of b <= a).
Student error: the parity loop stops one strike early, so a parity finding at the highest strike is never reported.
Student error: the discounted strike is truncated to whole cents before the parity gap.
Student error: the parity gap discounts the spot price (S df - K) instead of the strike (S - K df).
Student error: the convexity scan runs over every index after the first, including the last strike.
Student error: a convexity finding is netted against three legs at the fee only, without the half-spread.
Student error: the signed parity gap is rounded down (floor), so a negative gap rounds away from zero.
Parity explanation omits the cost-model label P6, so a parity finding does not name the cost it depends on.
Cost per finding charges the fee on three legs but ignores the half-spread, so a finding is netted against too little cost.
Scan discounts the strike with integer floor division, so the synthetic forward is truncated to whole cents before the gap.
Convexity finding kept when its net is exactly zero, because the convexity net test uses >= 0 instead of > 0.
Parity explanation names only P1, omitting P2, P3, the supplied discount factor P4 and the cost P6 it depends on.
Parity gross rounded with Python round(), which sends an exact half cent to the even cent, not up.
Convexity indices returned one-based (j + 1), so every convexity finding is attached to the next strike.
Findings returned with convexity records first, reversing the required parity-then-convexity order.
Parity gross taken as the magnitude of the signed half-up rounding, so a negative half cent rounds down in magnitude.
Convexity indices returned in decreasing order, largest strike first, against the increasing order the specification states.
Convexity scan starts at the second interior strike, so a violation at the first interior strike is never reported.
Parity explanation omits the no-income label P3, although the parity finding depends on it.
Convexity gross computed from the chord rounded to whole cents before the call is subtracted (double rounding).
Student error: the parity gap is cut to whole cents by int(), which truncates toward zero, not rounded.
Student error: the length check rejects a quote list that is shorter than the strikes, but not a longer one.
Student error: the gross amount of a finding is rounded up to the next whole cent, not to the nearest.
Student error: the convexity test counts a call that lies exactly on the chord as a violation, not only one above it.
Student error: the chord weights use the distance from the strike to its own neighbour, not to the other one.
Student error: a finding is kept when its net amount is zero or more, not only when it is strictly positive.
Student error: the half-spread is charged once per finding, while the fee is charged on each of the three legs.
Student error: the cost terms are validated only inside the branch that keeps a parity finding, so a negative
Student error: convexity_violations returns [] for a chain of fewer than three strikes before it checks df_ppm,
Student error: scan checks the quote-list lengths only for chains of two or more strikes, so a one-strike chain
Student error: the discounted strike K df is rounded to a whole cent before the parity gap is formed, so the gap is rounded twice.
Student error: the chord is rounded to a whole cent before the call is compared with it, so the convexity gross is taken from a rounded chord.
Student error: a convexity finding is charged two legs of cost, as if the wings were one call, instead of three calls.
Student error: a convexity finding is kept when its net amount is zero, while parity findings still need a strictly positive net.
Student error: parity_gap_cents rejects a strike of 1 cent, using strike < 2 as the test for a positive strike.
Student error: df_ppm = 1000000 is rejected, because the upper bound test uses < instead of <= (the range is 1 to 1000000).
Student error: a half-spread of exactly zero is rejected, because the cost check tests for a positive half-spread.
Student error: convexity_violations flags a call strictly below the chord, reversing the sign of the test.
Student error: convexity_violations raises the length error without naming the two lengths, although the spec says the message names them.
Student error: parity_gap_cents raises a different message for a zero strike, although the spec says it raises the same error as the other functions.
Student error: scan reports a convexity finding at the lower neighbour's strike, not at the interior strike whose call lies above the chord.
Student error: convexity_violations validates df_ppm with a message that does not name df_ppm, although the spec says each of the three functions names it.
Student error: convexity_violations flags a call that lies on the chord (zero second difference), although the spec says strictly above.
Student error: the strike error message says only that strikes must be strictly increasing, and omits the positive requirement the spec says the message states.
Student error: the df_ppm error message names df_ppm but not the range 1 to 1000000 that the spec says the message states.
